 17535                                  
 17536                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 17537                                  ; 21/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS - SYSINIT)
 17538                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 17539                                  
 17540                                  ;	MSStack.inc
 17541                                  ;
 17542                                  ;	Interrupt level 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7,(10, 11, 12, 14, 15 - AT level)
 17543                                  ;	should follow the standard Interrupt Sharing Scheme which has
 17544                                  ;	a standard header structure.
 17545                                  ;	Fyi, the following shows the relations between
 17546                                  ;	the interrupt vector and interrupt level.
 17547                                  ; VEC(Hex)    2  8  9  A  B  C	D  E  70  72  73  74  76  77
 17548                                  ; LVL(Deci)   9  0  1  2  3  4	5  6   8  10  11  12  14  15
 17549                                  ;	MSSTACK module modifies the following interrupt vectors
 17550                                  ;	to meet the standard Interrupt Sharing standard;
 17551                                  ;	  A, B, C, D, E, 72, 73, 74, 76, 77.
 17552                                  ;	Also, for interrupt level 7 and 15, the FirstFlag in a standard header
 17553                                  ;	should be initialized to indicat whether this interrupt handler is
 17554                                  ;	the first (= 80h) or not.  The FirstFlag entry of INT77h's
 17555                                  ;	program header is initialized in STKINIT.INC module.
 17556                                  ;	FirstFlag is only meaningful for interrupt level 7 and 15.
 17557                                  ;
 17558                                  
 17559                                  ;  User specifies the number of stack elements - default = 9
 17560                                  ;						 minimum = 8
 17561                                  ;						 maximum = 64
 17562                                  ;
 17563                                  ;  Intercepts Asynchronous Hardware Interrupts only
 17564                                  ;
 17565                                  ;  Picks a stack from pool of stacks and switches to it
 17566                                  ;
 17567                                  ;  Calls the previously saved interrupt vector after pushing flags
 17568                                  ;
 17569                                  ;  On return, returns the stack to the stack pool
 17570                                  ;
 17571                                  
 17572                                  ; This is a modification of STACKS:
 17573                                  ; 1. To fix a bug which was causing the program to take up too much space.
 17574                                  ; 2. To dispense stack space from hi-mem first rather than low-mem first.
 17575                                  ;    . Clobbers the stack that got too big instead of innocent stack
 17576                                  ;    . Allows system to work if the only stack that got too big was the most
 17577                                  ;      deeply nested one
 17578                                  ; 3. Disables NMI interrupts while setting the NMI vector.
 17579                                  ; 4. Does not intercept any interupts on a PCjr.
 17580                                  ; 5. Double checks that a nested interrupt didn't get the same stack.
 17581                                  ; 6. Intercepts Ints 70, 72-77 for PC-ATs and other future products
 17582                                  
 17583                                  		;EVEN
 17584                                  ;align 2
 17585                                  		; 21/10/2022
 17586                                  
 17587 00000000 0000                    		dw	0	; spare field but leave these in order
 17588 00000002 0000                    stackcount:	dw	0
 17589 00000004 0000                    stackat: 	dw	0
 17590 00000006 0000                    stacksize:	dw	0
 17591 00000008 0000                    stacks:		dw	0
 17592 0000000A 0000                    		dw	0
 17593                                  
 17594 0000000C [0800]                  firstentry:	dw	stacks
 17595 0000000E [4800]                  lastentry:	dw	stacks+(defaultcount*entrysize)-entrysize
 17596 00000010 [4800]                  nextentry:	dw	stacks+(defaultcount*entrysize)-entrysize
 17597

 17603 00000012 00000000                old02:	dd	0
 17604                                  
 17605                                  int02:
 17606                                  
 17607                                  ; *********************************************************************
 17608                                  ;
 17609                                  ; this is special support for the pc convertible / nmi handler
 17610                                  ;
 17611                                  ;	on the pc convertible, there is a situation where an nmi can be 
 17612                                  ;	caused by using the "out" instructions to certain ports. when this
 17613                                  ;	occurs, the pc convertible hardware *guarantees* that **nothing** 
 17614                                  ;	can stop the nmi or interfere with getting to the nmi handler. this
 17615                                  ;	includes other type of interrupts (hardware and software), and
 17616                                  ;	also includes other type of nmi's. when any nmi has occured,
 17617                                  ;	no other interrtupt (hardware, software or nmi) can occur until
 17618                                  ;	the software takes specific steps to allow further interrupting.
 17619                                  ;
 17620                                  ;	for pc convertible, the situation where the nmi is generated by the
 17621                                  ;	"out" to a control port requires "fixing-up" and re-attempting. in
 17622                                  ;	otherwords, it is actually a "restartable exception". in this
 17623                                  ;	case, the software handler must be able to get to the stack in
 17624                                  ;	order to figure out what instruction caused the problem, where
 17625                                  ;	it was "out"ing to and what value it was "out"ing.  therefore,
 17626                                  ;	we will not switch stacks in this situation. this situation is
 17627                                  ;	detected by interrogating port 62h, and checking for a bit value
 17628                                  ;	of 80h. if set, *****do not switch stacks*****.
 17629                                  ;
 17630                                  ; *********************************************************************
 17631                                  
 17632 00000016 50                      	push	ax
 17633 00000017 06                      	push	es
 17634 00000018 B800F0                  	mov	ax,0F000h
 17635 0000001B 8EC0                    	mov	es,ax

 17642                                  				; 0-3: values of DIP switches
 17643                                  				; 5: 1=Timer 2 channel out
 17644                                  				; 6: 1=I/O channel check
 17645                                  				; 7: 1=RAM parity check error occurred.
 17646 00000028 A880                    	test	al,80h
 17647 0000002A 7406                    	jz	short normal02

 17884                                  ;********************************************************************
 17885                                  
 17886                                  ; do interrupt stack switching. the fake return address holds
 17887                                  ; a pointer to the far-pointer of the actual interrupt
 17888                                  ; service routine
 17889                                  
 17890                                  ; 21/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT)
 17891                                  ; 21/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 17892                                  
 17893                                  ;allocbyte   equ 0
 17894                                  ;intlevel    equ 1
 17895                                  ;savedsp     equ 2
 17896                                  ;savedss     equ 4
 17897                                  ;newsp       equ 6
 17898                                  
 17899                                  do_int_stacks:
 17900 00000147 50                      	push	ax
 17901 00000148 55                      	push	bp
 17902 00000149 06                      	push	es
 17903 0000014A 2E8E06[0A00]            	mov	es,[cs:stacks+2]	; Get segment of stacks
 17904 0000014F 2E8B2E[1000]            	mov	bp,[cs:nextentry]	; get most likely candidate
 17905 00000154 B001                    	mov	al,allocated ; 1
 17906                                  	; 21/10/2022
 17907                                  	;xchg	[es:bp+allocbyte],al
 17908                                  	; 11/12/2022
 17909 00000156 26864600                	xchg	[es:bp],al		; grab the entry
 17910 0000015A 3C00                    	cmp	al,free ; 0		; still avail?
 17911 0000015C 754F                    	jne	short notfree02
 17912                                  
 17913 0000015E 2E832E[1000]08          	sub	word [cs:nextentry],entrysize ; set for next interrupt
 17914                                  
 17915                                  found02:
 17916 00000164 26896602                	mov	[es:bp+savedsp],sp	; save sp value
 17917 00000168 268C5604                	mov	[es:bp+savedss],ss	; save ss also
 17918                                  
 17919 0000016C 89E8                    	mov	ax,bp			; temp save of table offset
 17920                                  
 17921 0000016E 268B6E06                	mov	bp,[es:bp+newsp]	; get new SP value
 17922                                  	; 21/10/2022
 17923                                  	;mov	bp,[es:bp+6]
 17924                                  	; 11/12/2022
 17925                                  	;cmp	[es:bp+0],ax
 17926 00000172 26394600                	cmp	[es:bp],ax		; check for offset into table
 17927 00000176 7542                    	jne	short foundbad02
 17928                                  
 17929                                  	;mov	ax,es			; point ss,sp to the new stack
 17930                                  	;mov	es,bp
 17931                                  	;mov	bp,sp
 17932                                  	;mov	bp,[bp+6]
 17933                                  	;mov	ss,ax
 17934                                  	;mov	sp,es
 17935                                  	;mov	es,ax
 17936                                  	;mov	bp,[cs:bp]

 17938                                  	; 21/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 code SYSINIT code)
 17939 00000178 55                      	push    bp
 17940 00000179 89E5                    	mov     bp,sp
 17941 0000017B 8B4608                  	mov     ax,[bp+8]
 17942 0000017E 5D                      	pop     bp

 17951 00000189 9C                      	pushf				; go execute the real interrupt handler
 17952                                  	; 11/12/2022

 19263                                  ; to install the low memory stub (this must be done before allowing any

 19265                                  ; call dos_segreinit at all, since the interrupt vector table has already 
 19266                                  ; been patched.

 19569                                  ; we are going to open the command interpreter and size it as is done in
 19570                                  ; ldfil. the reason we must do this is that sysinit is in free memory. if
 19571                                  ; there is not enough room for the command interpreter,exec will probably
 19572                                  ; overlay our stack and code so when it returns with an error sysinit won't be
 19573                                  ; here to catch it. this code is not perfect (for instance .exe command
 19574                                  ; interpreters are possible) because it does its sizing based on the
 19575                                  ; assumption that the file being loaded is a .com file. it is close enough to
 19576                                  ; correctness to be usable.

 19605                                  ; unallocated memory (as of the Dealloc of [area], above). This is ideal

 19607                                  ; anyway, and no one has responsibility for freeing "config_wrkseg". But
 19608                                  ; we need to make sure that there's no way Exec will stomp on that data
 19609                                  ; before it can copy it, and one way to do that is to make the available
 19610                                  ; memory calculation even more "paranoid", by subtracting "config_wrkseg"
 19611                                  ; from the "memory_size" segment value (which is typically A000h) instead
 19612                                  ; of the current sysinit CS....

 20391                                  ; BUGBUG -- 5 Aug 92 -- chuckst -- Allocating space for DOS
 20392                                  ;	  using DOS itself causes an arena to be generated.
 20393                                  ;	  Unfortunately, certain programs (like PROTMAN$)
 20394                                  ;	  assume that the device drivers are loaded into
 20395                                  ;	  the first arena. For this reason, MagicDrv's
 20396                                  ;	  main device driver header arena is manually
 20397                                  ;	  truncated from the arena chain, and the space
 20398                                  ;	  for DOS is allocated using the following
 20399                                  ;	  simple code, which also assumes that the
 20400                                  ;	  first arena is the free one where DOS's low
 20401                                  ;	  stub will go.
 20402                                  ;
 20403                                  ; M012 : BEGIN
 20404                                  
 20405                                  	; 23/10/2022
 20406                                  update_arena:
 20407 0000096C 1E                      	push	ds ; ds = cs
 20408 0000096D 57                      	push	di
 20409 0000096E 51                      	push	cx
 20410 0000096F 52                      	push	dx
 20411                                  	; 23/10/2022
 20412                                  	;lds	di,[cs:DOSINFO]			; get ptr to DOS var
 20413                                  	; 11/12/2022
 20414                                  	; ds = cs 
 20415 00000970 C53E[6B02]              	lds	di,[DOSINFO] ; 27/03/2019	
 20416 00000974 4F                      	dec	di
 20417 00000975 4F                      	dec	di				; Arena head is immediately
 20418                                  						;  before sysvar
 20419 00000976 8E05                    	mov	es,[di]				; es = arena head
 20420                                  	;mov	cx,[es:ARENA.SIZE]		; cx = total low mem size
 20421 00000978 268B0E0300              	mov	cx,[es:3]
 20422 0000097D 39D9                    	cmp	cx,bx				; is it sufficient ?
 20423 0000097F 7227                    	jb	short FatalErr			; no, fatal error
 20424                                  
 20425                                  	;mov	dl,[es:ARENA.SIGNATURE]
 20426 00000981 268A160000              	mov	dl,[es:0]
 20427 00000986 8CC0                    	mov	ax,es
 20428 00000988 01D8                    	add	ax,bx				; ax = new arena head
 20429 0000098A 8905                    	mov	[di],ax				; store it in DOS data area
 20430 0000098C 8ED8                    	mov	ds,ax
 20431                                  	;mov	[ARENA.SIGNATURE],dl		; type of arena
 20432 0000098E 88160000                	mov	[0],dl
 20433                                  	;mov	word [ARENA.OWNER],0		; free
 20434 00000992 C70601000000            	mov	word [1],0

 20439                                  	; 23/10/2022

 20470                                  ;	grab_the_hma tries to enable a20 and make sure there is memory
 20471                                  ;	  up there. If it gets any sort of error, it will return with
 20472                                  ;	  carry set so that we can resort to running low.

 20639                                  ; following piece of code will be moved into a para boundary. And the para

 20642                                  ; to determine free extended memory.

 20655

 20658 00000A32 0000                    	dw	0		; strategy routine offset
 20659 00000A34 0000                    	dw	0		; interrupt routine offset

 21911                                  ;global rearm command for shared interrupt devices attached in the system;
 21912                                  ;shared interrupt attachment has some problem when it issues interrupt
 21913                                  ;during a warm reboot. once the interrupt is presented by the attachment,
 21914                                  ;no further interrupts on that level will be presented until a global rearm
 21915                                  ;is issued. by the request of the system architecture group, msbio will
 21916                                  ;issue a global rearm after every device driver is loaded.
 21917                                  ;to issue a global rearm:	;for pc1,xt,palace
 21918                                  ;
 21919                                  ;			  out 02f2h,xx  ; interrupt level 2
 21920                                  ;			  out 02f3h,xx  ; interrupt level 3

 21922                                  ;			  out 02f5h,xx  ; interrupt level 5
 21923                                  ;			  out 02f6h,xx  ; interrupt level 6

 21930                                  ;			  out 06f3h,xx  ; interrupt level 11

 21932                                  ;			  out 06f6h,xx  ; interrupt level 14
 21933                                  ;			  out 06f7h,xx  ; interrupt level 15

 22300                                  ;	ParaRound rounds a byte count up to a multiple of 16, then divides
 22301                                  ;	by 16 yielding a "length in paragraphs" value.

 22315                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 22316                                  ; sysinit_base module.
 22317                                  ;
 22318                                  ; This module is relocated by the routine EndFile to a location in low
 22319                                  ; memory. It is then called by SYSINIT to perform the EXEC of programs
 22320                                  ; that are being loaded by the "install=" command. After the EXEC call
 22321                                  ; completes, this module performs a checksum on the SYSINIT code (at the
 22322                                  ; top of memory) to be sure that the EXECed program did not damage it.
 22323                                  ; If it did, then this module will print an error message and stop the
 22324                                  ; system. Otherwise, it returns control to SYSINIT.
 22325                                  ;
 22326                                  ;in: after relocation,
 22327                                  ;    ax = 4b00h - load and execute the program dos function.
 22328                                  ;    ds = confbot. segment of config.sys file image
 22329                                  ;    es = sysinitseg. segment of sysinit module itself.
 22330                                  ;    ds:dx = pointer to asciiz string of the path,filename to be executed.
 22331                                  ;    es:bx = pointer to a parameter block for load.
 22332                                  ;    SI_end (byte) - offset vaule of end of sysinit module label
 22333                                  ;    bigsize (word) - # of word from confbot to SI_end.
 22334                                  ;    chksum (word) - sum of every byte from confbot to SI_end in a
 22335                                  ;			word boundary moduler form.
 22336                                  ;    sysinit_ptr (dword ptr) - return address to sysinit module.
 22337                                  ;
 22338                                  ;note: sysinit should save necessary registers and when the control is back
 22339                                  
 22340                                  	; 24/10/2022
 22341                                  	; (SYSINIT:115Ch for MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT)
 22342                                  sysinit_base:				
 22343 0000109D 2E8C166200              	mov	[cs:sysinit_base_ss],ss	; save stack
 22344 000010A2 2E89266400              	mov	[cs:sysinit_base_sp],sp	
 22345 000010A7 CD21                    	int	21h			; load/exec dos call.
 22346 000010A9 2E8E166200              	mov	ss,[cs:sysinit_base_ss]	; restore stack
 22347 000010AE 2E8B266400              	mov	sp,[cs:sysinit_base_sp]
 22348 000010B3 1F                      	pop	ds			; restore confbot seg
 22349 000010B4 07                      	pop	es			; restore sysinitseg
 22350 000010B5 7216                    	jc	short sysinit_base_end	; load/exec function failed.
 22351                                  					; at this time,i don't have to worry about
 22352                                  					; that sysinit module has been broken or not.
 22353 000010B7 E81800                  	call	sum_up			; otherwise,check if it is good.
 22354 000010BA 263906[5603]            	cmp	[es:checksum],ax
 22355 000010BF 740C                    	je	short sysinit_base_end
 22356                                  
 22357                                  ;	memory broken. show "memory allocation error" message and stall.
 22358                                  
 22359 000010C1 B409                    	mov	ah,9
 22360 000010C3 0E                      	push	cs
 22361 000010C4 1F                      	pop	ds
 22362 000010C5 BA6600                  	mov	dx,mem_alloc_err_msgx-sysinit_base ; 65h (for MSDOS 5.0 SYSINIT)
 22363 000010C8 CD21                    	int	21h
 22364                                  		; DOS - PRINT STRING
 22365                                  		; DS:DX -> string terminated by "$"
 22366                                  	; 24/10/2022
 22367                                  _stall: 
 22368                                  	; 11/12/2022
 22369 000010CA F4                      	hlt 
 22370                                  	; 02/11/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 22371                                  	;hlt				;use HLT to minimize energy consumption
 22372 000010CB EBFD                            jmp	short _stall
 22373                                  
 22374                                  sysinit_base_end: 
 22375 000010CD 26FF2E[5203]            	jmp	far [es:sysinit_ptr]	;return back to sysinit module

 22385                                  ;	 sysinit segment,the data area, and the current stack area are not
 22386                                  ;	 coverd. in this sense,this check sum routine only gives a minimal
 22387                                  ;	 gaurantee to be safe.

 22389                                  ;first sum up confbot seg.
 22390

 22397 000010DB 31C0                    	xor	ax,ax

 22399                                  					;whole test better fail.
 22400 000010E2 D1E9                    	shr	cx,1			; make it a word count
 22401 000010E4 7406                    	jz	short sum_sys_code	; when config.sys file not exist.

 22596                                  ; ======================================================================
 22597                                  ; MSSTACK initialization routine - MSDOS 6.0 - SYSDINIT1.ASM - 1991
 22598                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 22599                                  ; 27/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 22600                                  
 22601                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 22602                                  ; ibmstack initialization routine.
 22603                                  ;
 22604                                  ;	to follow the standard interrupt sharing scheme, msstack.asm
 22605                                  ;	has been modified. this initialization routine also has to
 22606                                  ;	be modified because for the interrupt level 7 and 15, firstflag
 22607                                  ;	should be set to signal that this interrupt handler is the
 22608                                  ;	first handler hooked to this interrupt vector.
 22609                                  ;	we determine this by looking at the instruction pointed by
 22610                                  ;	this vector. if it is iret, then this handler should be the
 22611                                  ;	first one. in our case, only the interrupt vector 77h is the
 22612                                  ;	interrupt level 15. (we don't hook interrupt level 7.)
 22613                                  ;
 22614                                  ;	the followings are mainly due to m.r.t; ptm fix of p886 12/3/86
 22615                                  ;	some design changes are needed to the above interrupt sharing
 22616                                  ;	method. the above sharing scheme assumes that 1). interrupt
 22617                                  ;	sharing is never done on levels that have bios support. 2). "phantom"
 22618                                  ;	interrupts would only be generated on levels 7 and 15.
 22619                                  ;	these assumptions are not true any more. we have to use the firstflag
 22620                                  ;	for every level of interrupt. we will set the firstflag on the following
 22621                                  ;	conditions:
 22622                                  ;
 22623                                  ;	 a.	 if the cs portion of the vector is 0000, then "first"
 22624                                  ;	 b. else if cs:ip points to valid shared header, then not "first"
 22625                                  ;	 c. else if cs:ip points to an iret, then "first"
 22626                                  ;	 d. else if cs:ip points to dummy, then "first"
 22627                                  ;
 22628                                  ;	where dummy is - the cs portion must be f000, and the ip portion must
 22629                                  ;	be equal to the value at f000:ff01. this location is the initial value
 22630                                  ;	from vector_table for interrupt 7, one of the preserved addresses in all
 22631                                  ;	the bioses for all of the machines.
 22632                                  ;
 22633                                  ;	system design group requests bios to handle the phantom interrupts.
 22634                                  ;
 22635                                  ;	the "phantom" interrupt is an illegal interrupt such as an interrupt
 22636                                  ;	produced by the bogus adapter card even without interrupt request is
 22637                                  ;	set.  more specifically, 1). the 8259 has a feature when running in
 22638                                  ;	edge triggered mode to latch a pulse and present the interrupt when
 22639                                  ;	the processor indicates interrupt acknowledge (inta). the interrupt
 22640                                  ;	pulse was exist at the time of inta to get a "phantom" interrupt.
 22641                                  ;	2). or, this is caused by adapter cards placing a glitch on the
 22642                                  ;	interrupt line.
 22643                                  ;
 22644                                  ;	to handle those "phantom" interrupts, the main stack code will check
 22645                                  ;	the own firstflag, and if it is not "first" (which means the forward
 22646                                  ;	pointer points to the legal shared interrupt handler), then pass the
 22647                                  ;	control. if it is the first, then the following action should be
 22648                                  ;	taken. we don't have to implement skack logic in this case.
 22649                                  ;
 22650                                  ;	to implement this logic, we rather choose a simple method.
 22651                                  ;	if ont of the above "firstflag" conditions is met, we are not
 22652                                  ;	going to hook this interrupt vector. the reason is if the original
 22653                                  ;	vector points to "iret" and do nothing, we don't need
 22654                                  ;	to implement the stack logic for it. this will simplify implementation
 22655                                  ;	while maintaining compatibility with the old version of dos.
 22656                                  ;	this implies that in the main stack code, there might be a stack code
 22657                                  ;	that will never be used, a dead code.
 22658                                  ;
 22659                                  ;in - cs, ds -> sysinitseg, es -> relocated stack code & data.
 22660                                  
 22661                                  	; 25/10/2022 - Retro DOS 4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS, SYSINIT)
 22662                                  	; (SYSINIT:1287h)
 22663                                  
 22664                                  	; 14/12/2022
 22665                                  stackinit:

 23506                                  ; 25/10/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS, SYSINIT)
 23507                                  ; (SYSINIT:1610h)
 23508                                  
 23509                                  new_init_loop:
 23510                                  
 23511                                  ;input: si=ofset into vector table of the particular int vector being adjusted
 23512                                  ;	bx=ds:offset of oldxx, where will be saved the pointer to original owner
 23513                                  ;	dx=ds:offset of intxx, the new interrupt handler
 23514                                  ;	di=offset value of int19old&aa variable in bios.
 23515                                  ;	es=zero, segid of vector table
 23516                                  ;	ds=relocated stack code segment
 23517                                  
 23518                                  ; 13/04/2024
 23519                                  %if 0
 23520                                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;remember offset in vector
 23521                                  	mov	[bx],ax			; to original owner in ds
 23522                                  	mov	ax,[es:si+2]		;remember segid in vector
 23523                                  	mov	[bx+2],ax		; to original owner in ds
 23524                                  
 23525                                  	push	ds
 23526                                  	;;mov	ax,Bios_Data ; 70h
 23527                                  	;mov	ax,KERNEL_SEGMENT ; 70h
 23528                                  	; 21/10/2022
 23529                                  	mov	ax,DOSBIODATASEG ; 0070h
 23530                                  	mov	ds,ax			;set int19oldxx value in bios for
 23531                                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;int 19 handler
 23532                                  	mov	[di],ax
 23533                                  	mov	ax,[es:si+2]
 23534                                  	mov	[di+2],ax
 23535                                  	pop	ds
 23536                                  %else
 23537                                  	; 13/04/2024 - Retro DOS v4.1
 23538 000013B7 1E                      	push	ds
 23539 000013B8 268B4402                	mov	ax,[es:si+2]		;remember segid in vector
 23540 000013BC 894702                  	mov	[bx+2],ax		; to original owner in ds
 23541 000013BF 50                      	push	ax
 23542 000013C0 268B04                  	mov	ax,[es:si]		;remember offset in vector
 23543 000013C3 8907                    	mov	[bx],ax			; to original owner in ds
 23544 000013C5 50                      	push	ax
 23545 000013C6 B87000                  	mov	ax,DOSBIODATASEG ; 0070h
 23546 000013C9 8ED8                    	mov	ds,ax			;set int19oldxx value in bios for
 23547 000013CB 58                      	pop	ax			;int 19 handler
 23548 000013CC 8905                    	mov	[di],ax
 23549 000013CE 58                      	pop	ax
 23550 000013CF 894502                  	mov	[di+2],ax
 23551 000013D2 1F                      	pop	ds
 23552                                  %endif
 23553 000013D3 268914                  	mov	[es:si],dx  	;set vector to point to new int handler
 23554 000013D6 268C5C02                	mov	[es:si+2],ds
 23555 000013DA C3                      	retn

 23828                                  ;		DW	CONTROL 	; DESCRIPTION OF SWITCH 1
 23829                                  ;		:			; REPEATS maxs-1 TIMES
 23830                                  ;		DB	maxk		; # OF KEYWORD
 23831                                  ;		DW	CONTROL 	; DESCRIPTION OF KEYWORD 1
 23832                                  ;		:			; REPEATS maxk-1 TIMES
 23833                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 23834                                  
 23835                                  ;-------------------------------- PARMSX block structure
 23836                                  struc _$P_PARMSX_Blk		;AN000;
 23837 00000000 ??                       .MinP: resb 1			;AN000; Minimum positional number
 23838 00000001 ??                       .MaxP:	resb 1			;AN000; Maximum positional number
 23839 00000002 ????                     .1st_Control: resw 1		;AN000; Address of the 1st CONTROL block
 23840                                  endstruc
 23841                                  
 23842                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 23843                                  ; << Control field definition  >>
 23844                                  ;
 23845                                  ;
 23846                                  ;CONTROL   LABEL   BYTE
 23847                                  ;	   DW	   MATCH_FLAGS	   ; CONTROLS TYPE MATCHED
 23848                                  ;				   ; 8000H=NUMERIC VALUE, (VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 23849                                  ;				   ; 4000H=SIGNED NUMERIC VALUE (VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 23850                                  ;				   ; 2000H=SIMPLE STRING(VALUE LIST WILL BE CHECKED)
 23851                                  ;				   ; 1000H=DATE STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23852                                  ;				   ; 0800H=TIME STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23853                                  ;				   ; 0400H=COMPLEX LIST (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23854                                  ;				   ; 0200H=FILE SPEC (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23855                                  ;				   ; 0100H=DRIVE ONLY (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23856                                  ;				   ; 0080H=QUOTED STRING (VALUE LIST WON'T BE CHECKED)
 23857                                  ;				   ; 0010H=IGNORE ":" AT END IN MATCH
 23858                                  ;				   ; 0002H=REPEATS ALLOWED
 23859                                  ;				   ; 0001H=OPTIONAL
 23860                                  ;	   DW	   FUNCTION_FLAGS
 23861                                  ;				   ; 0001H=CAP RESULT BY FILE TABLE
 23862                                  ;				   ; 0002H=CAP RESULT BY CHAR TABLE
 23863                                  ;				   ; 0010H=REMOVE ":" AT END
 23864                                  ; (tm10)			   ; 0020H=colon is not necessary for switch
 23865                                  ;	   DW	   RESULT	   ; RESULT BUFFER
 23866                                  ;	   DW	   VALUES	   ; VALUE LISTS
 23867                                  ;	   DB	   nid		   ; NUMBER OF KEYWORD/SWITCH SYNONYMS IN FOLLOWING LIST
 23868                                  ;	   DB	   "...",0         ; IF n >0, KEYWORD 1
 23869                                  ;	   :
 23870                                  ;
 23871                                  ;Note:
 23872                                  ;    - The MATCH_FLAG is bit significant. You can set, for example, TIME bit and
 23873                                  ;      DATE bit simalteniously.
 23874                                  ;
 23875                                  ;      The parser examins each bit along with the following priority.
 23876                                  ;
 23877                                  ;      COMPLEX -> DATE -> TIME -> NUMERIC VAL -> SIGNED NUMERIC VAL -> DRIVE ->
 23878                                  ;      FILE SPEC -> SIMPLE STRING.
 23879                                  ;
 23880                                  ;    - When the FUNCTION_FLAG is 0001 or 0002, the STRING pointed to by a pointer
 23881                                  ;      in the result buffer is capitalized.
 23882                                  ;
 23883                                  ;    - Match_Flags 0001H and 0002H have meaning only for the positional.
 23884                                  ;
 23885                                  ;    - The "...",0 (bottom most line) does require '=' or '/'. When you need a
 23886                                  ;      switch, for example, '/A', then STRING points to;
 23887                                  ;
 23888                                  ;			DB    1 	; number of following synonyms
 23889                                  ;			DB   '/A',0
 23890                                  ;
 23891                                  ;      When you need a keyword, for example, 'CODEPAGE=', then "...",0 will be;
 23892                                  ;
 23893                                  ;			DB    1 	; number of following synonyms
 23894                                  ;			DB   'CODEPAGE=',0
 23895                                  ;
 23896                                  ;    - "..." must consist of upper case characters only because the parser
 23897                                  ;      performs pattern matching after converting input to upper case (by
 23898                                  ;      using the current country upper case table)
 23899                                  ;
 23900                                  ;    - One "..." can contain only one switch or keyword. If you need, for
 23901                                  ;      example /A and /B, the format will be;
 23902                                  ;
 23903                                  ;			DB    2 	; number of following synonyms
 23904                                  ;			DB    '/A',0
 23905                                  ;			DB    '/B',0
 23906                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 23907                                  
 23908                                  ;**** Match_Flags
 23909                                  
 23910                                  _$P_Num_Val	   equ	8000h		;AN000; Numeric Value
 23911                                  _$P_SNum_Val	   equ	4000h		;AN000; Signed numeric value
 23912                                  _$P_Simple_S	   equ	2000h		;AN000; Simple string
 23913                                  _$P_Date_S	   equ	1000h		;AN000; Date string
 23914                                  _$P_Time_S	   equ	0800h		;AN000; Time string
 23915                                  _$P_Cmpx_S	   equ	0400h		;AN000; Complex string
 23916                                  _$P_File_Spc	   equ	0200h		;AN000; File Spec
 23917                                  _$P_Drv_Only	   equ	0100h		;AN000; Drive Only
 23918                                  _$P_Qu_String	   equ	0080h		;AN000; Quoted string
 23919                                  _$P_Ig_Colon	   equ	0010h		;AN000; Ignore colon at end in match
 23920                                  _$P_Repeat	   equ	0002h		;AN000; Repeat allowed
 23921                                  _$P_Optional	   equ	0001h		;AN000; Optional
 23922                                  
 23923                                  ;**** Function flags
 23924                                  
 23925                                  _$P_CAP_File	   equ	0001h		;AN000; CAP result by file table
 23926                                  _$P_CAP_Char	   equ	0002h		;AN000; CAP result by character table
 23927                                  _$P_Rm_Colon	   equ	0010h		;AN000; Remove ":" at the end
 23928                                  _$P_colon_is_not_necessary equ 0020h	;AN000;(tm10) /+10 and /+:10
 23929

 23931                                  struc _$P_Control_Blk
 23932 00000000 ????                     .Match_Flag:	 resw 1		;AN000; Controls type matched
 23933 00000002 ????                     .Function_Flag: resw 1		;AN000; Function should be taken
 23934 00000004 ????                     .Result_Buf:	 resw 1		; Result buffer address
 23935 00000006 ????                     .Value_List:	 resw 1		;AN000; Value list address
 23936 00000008 ??                       .nid:		 resb 1		;AN000; # of keyword/SW synonyms
 23937 00000009 ??                       .KEYorSW:	 resb 1		;AN000; keyword or sw
 23938                                  endstruc
 23939                                  
 23940                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 23941                                  ; << Value List Definition >>
 23942                                  ;
 23943                                  ;VALUES 	LABEL	BYTE
 23944                                  ;		DB	nval			; NUMBER OF VALUE DEFINITIONS (0 - 3)
 23945                                  ;	     +-
 23946                                  ;	     |	DB	nrng			; NUMBER OF RANGES
 23947                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF RANGE MATCHED
 23948                                  ;	     | +DD	X,Y			; RANGE OF VALUES
 23949                                  ;	     |	:
 23950                                  ;	     |	DB	nnval			; NUMBER OF CHOICES
 23951                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF NUMBER CHOICE MATCHED
 23952                                  ;	     | +DD	VALUE			; SPECIFIC CHOICE IF NUMBER
 23953                                  ;	     |	:
 23954                                  ;	     |	DB	nstrval 		; NUMBER OF CHOICES
 23955                                  ;	     | +DB	ITEM_TAG		; RETURN VALUE IF STRING CHOICE MATCHED
 23956                                  ;	     | +DW	STRING			; SPECIFIC CHOICE IF STING
 23957                                  ;	     +-	:
 23958                                  ;
 23959                                  ;STRING 	DB	"...",0                 ; ASCIIZ STRING IMAGE
 23960                                  ;
 23961                                  ;Note:
 23962                                  ;    - ITEM_TAG must not be 0FFH, which will be used in the result buffer
 23963                                  ;      when no choice lists are provided.
 23964                                  ;
 23965                                  ;    - STRING must consist of upper case characters only because the parser
 23966                                  ;      performs pattern matching after converting input to upper case (by
 23967                                  ;      using the current country upper case table)
 23968                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 23969                                  
 23970                                  _$P_nval_None	   equ	0		;AN000; no value list ID
 23971                                  _$P_nval_Range	   equ	1		;AN000; range list ID
 23972                                  _$P_nval_Value	   equ	2		;AN000; value list ID
 23973                                  _$P_nval_String	   equ	3		;AN000; string list ID
 23974                                  _$P_Len_Range	   equ	9		;AN000; Length of a range choice(two DD plus one DB)
 23975                                  _$P_Len_Value	   equ	5		;AN000; Length of a value choice(one DD plus one DB)
 23976                                  _$P_Len_String	   equ	3		;AN000; Length of a string choice(one DW plus one DB)
 23977                                  _$P_No_nrng	   equ	0		;AN000; (tm07) no nrng. nnval must not be 0.
 23978

 23980 00000000 ??                       .NumofList: resb 1			;AN000; number of following choice
 23981 00000001 ????                     .Val_XL:    resw 1			;AN000; lower word of value
 23982 00000003 ????                     .Val_XH:    resw 1			;AN000; higher word of value
 23983 00000005 ????                     .Val_YL:    resw 1			;AN000; lower word of another value
 23984 00000007 ????                     .Val_YH:    resw 1			;AN000; higher word of another value
 23985                                  endstruc

 23987                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 23988                                  ; << Result Buffer Definition  >>
 23989                                  ;
 23990                                  ;RESULT 	LABEL	BYTE			; BELOW FILLED IN FOR DEFAULTS
 23991                                  ;		DB	type			; TYPE RETURNED: 0=RESERVED,
 23992                                  ;						;	1=NUMBER, 2=LIST INDEX,
 23993                                  ;						;	3=STRING, 4=COMPLEX,
 23994                                  ;						;	5=FILESPEC, 6=DRIVE
 23995                                  ;						;	7=DATE, 8=TIME
 23996                                  ;						;	9=QUOTED STRING
 23997                                  ;		DB	ITEM_TAG		; MATCHED ITEM TAG
 23998                                  ;
 23999                                  ;		dw	synonym@		; es:@ points to found SYNONYM if provided.
 24000                                  ;
 24001                                  ;            +-
 24002                                  ;	    | DD	n			; VALUE IF NUMBER
 24003                                  ;	    | or
 24004                                  ;	    |	DW	i			; INDEX (OFFSET) INTO VALUE LIST
 24005                                  ;	    |					; (ES presents Segment address)
 24006                                  ;	    | or
 24007                                  ;	    |	DD	STRING			; OFFSET OF STRING VALUE
 24008                                  ;	    | or
 24009                                  ;	    |	DB	drv			; DRIVE NUMBER (1-A, 2-B,..., 26-Z)
 24010                                  ;	    | or
 24011                                  ;	    |	DW	YEAR	   ;(1980-2099)  IN CASE OF DATE
 24012                                  ;	    |	DB	MONTH	   ;(1-12)	 Note: Range check is not performed.
 24013                                  ;	    |	DB	DATE	   ;(1-31)	       0 is filled when the corresponding field was not specified.
 24014                                  ;	    | or
 24015                                  ;	    |	DB	HOUR	   ;(0-23)	  IN CASE OF TIME
 24016                                  ;	    |	DB	MINUTES    ;(0-59)	  Note: Range check is not performed .
 24017                                  ;	    |	DB	SECONDS    ;(0-59)		0 is filled when the corresponding field was not specified .
 24018                                  ;	    |	DB	HUNDREDTHS ;(0-99)
 24019                                  ;	    +-
 24020                                  ;
 24021                                  ;
 24022                                  ;Note: ITEM_TAG is 0FFH when the caller does not specify the choice
 24023                                  ;      list.
 24024                                  ;
 24025                                  ;      YEAR: If the input value for the year is less than 100, parser
 24026                                  ;	     adds 1900 to it.  For example, when 87 is input to parser for
 24027                                  ;	     the year value, he returns 1987.
 24028                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 24151                                  ;***********************************************************************
 24152                                  ; SysParse;
 24153                                  ;
 24154                                  ;  Function : Parser Entry
 24155                                  ;
 24156                                  ;  Input: DS:SI -> command line
 24157                                  ;	  ES:DI -> parameter block
 24158                                  ;	  cs -> psdata.inc
 24159                                  ;	  CX = operand ordinal
 24160                                  ;
 24161                                  ;	  Note:  ES is the segment containing all the control blocks defined
 24162                                  ;		 by the caller, except for the DOS COMMAND line parms, which
 24163                                  ;		 is in DS.
 24164                                  ;
 24165                                  ;  Output: CY = 1   error of caller, means invalid parameter block or
 24166                                  ;		    invalid value list. But this parser does NOT implement
 24167                                  ;		    this feature. Therefore CY always zero.
 24168                                  ;
 24169                                  ;	   CY = 0   AX = return code
 24170                                  ;		    BL = terminated delimiter code
 24171                                  ;		    CX = new operand ordinal
 24172                                  ;		    SI = set past scaned operand
 24173                                  ;		    DX = selected result buffer
 24174                                  ;
 24175                                  ; Use:	_$P_Skip_Delim, _$P_Chk_EOL, _$P_Chk_Delim, _$P_Chk_DBCS
 24176                                  ;	_$P_Chk_Swtch, _$P_Chk_Pos_Control, _$P_Chk_Key_Control
 24177                                  ;	_$P_Chk_Sw_Control, _$P_Fill_Result
 24178                                  ;
 24179                                  ; Vars: _$P_Ordinal(RW), _$P_RC(RW), _$P_SI_Save(RW), _$P_DX(R), _$P_Terminator(R)
 24180                                  ;	_$P_SaveSI_Cmpx(W), _$P_Flags(RW), _$P_Found_SYNONYM(R), _$P_Save_EOB(W)
 24181                                  ;
 24182                                  ;-------- Modification History -----------------------------------------
 24183                                  ;
 24184                                  ;  4/04/87 : Created by K. K,
 24185                                  ;  4/28/87 : _$P_Val_YH assemble error (tm01)
 24186                                  ;	   : JMP SHORT assemble error (tm02)
 24187                                  ;  5/14/87 : Someone doesn't want to include psdata (tm03)
 24188                                  ;  6/12/87 : _$P_Bridge is missing when TimeSw equ 0 and (CmpxSw equ 1 or
 24189                                  ;	     DateSW equ 1)	      (tm04)
 24190                                  ;  6/12/87 : _$P_SorD_Quote is missing when QusSw equ 0 and CmpxSW equ 1
 24191                                  ;				      (tm05) in PSDATA.INC
 24192                                  ;  6/12/87 : _$P_FileSp_Char and _$P_FileSP_Len are missing
 24193                                  ;	     when FileSW equ 0 and DrvSW equ 1 (tm06) in PSDATA.INC

 24226                                  ;
 24227                                  
 24228                                  ;  8/28/87 : Ed K, Kerry S (;AN020;)

 24855                                  ;
 24856                                  ; Input:    AH = Item tag

 24859                                  ;		  AL = 2: DX has index(offset) into value list
 24860                                  ;		  AL = 6: DL has driver # (1-A, 2-B, ... , 26 - Z)
 24861                                  ;		  AL = 7: DX has year, CL has month and CH has date
 24862                                  ;		  AL = 8: DL has hours, DH has minutes, CL has seconds,
 24863                                  ;			  amd CH has hundredths

 24964                                  ; _$P_Check_Match_Flags
 24965                                  ;
 24966                                  ; Function:  Check the mutch_flags and make the exit code and set the
 24967                                  ;	     result buffer
 24968                                  ;
 24969                                  ;	    Check for types in this order:
 24970                                  ;		Complex
 24971                                  ;		Date
 24972                                  ;		Time
 24973                                  ;		Drive
 24974                                  ;		Filespec
 24975                                  ;		Quoted String
 24976                                  ;		Simple String

 26272                                  ;		 position, or is a slash but may be part of a date string, i.e.

 26961                                  
 26962                                  ;include	highvar.inc	; devicehigh variables (used by loadhigh also)
 26963                                  
 26964                                  ; 30/03/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 26965                                  ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 26966                                  
 26967                                  ;   Module:   HIGHVAR.INC - Data common to LOADHIGH and DEVICEHIGH, res seg
 26968                                  ;
 26969                                  ;   Date:     May 14, 1992
 26970                                  ;
 26971                                  ;******************************************************************************
 26972                                  ;
 26973                                  ;   Modification log:
 26974                                  ;
 26975                                  ;     DATE    WHO      DESCRIPTION
 26976                                  ;   --------  -------  --------------------------------------------------------
 26977                                  ;   05/14/92  t-richj  Original
 26978                                  ;   06/21/92  t-richj  Final revisions before check-in
 26979                                  ;
 26980                                  ;******************************************************************************
 26981                                  ;
 26982                                  ; There are two primary definitions which need to be made, selectively, before
 26983                                  ; this include file should be used.  These are:
 26984                                  ;    HV_Extern - If this has been defined, variables for this module will be
 26985                                  ;                declared as external.  Otherwise, variables will be declared
 26986                                  ;                public, as well as defined, here.  LoadHigh declares HV_Extern
 26987                                  ;                in stub.asm and loadhi.asm, and does not declare it in
 26988                                  ;                rdata.asm... DeviceHigh does not declare HV_Extern anywhere
 26989                                  ;                (as only one module, sysconf.asm, includes this file).
 26990                                  ;    HV_LoadHigh - This should be defined when this module is going into
 26991                                  ;                  command.com, for LoadHigh.  All of loadhi.asm, stub.asm and
 26992                                  ;                  rdata.asm define this, while io.sys' sysconf.asm does not.
 26993                                  ;
 26994                                  ;******************************************************************************
 26995                                  
 26996                                  ; To keep track of which UMBs were specified on the DH/LH command lines, and
 26997                                  ; to keep track of the minimum sizes given for each, there're two arrays kept
 26998                                  ; in { IO.SYS: sysinitseg / COMMAND.COM: DATARES }... each is MAXUMB elements
 26999                                  ; big.  16 should be around 14 too many for most users, so there's no expected
 27000                                  ; space problem (it's just such a nice round number, eh?).
 27001                                  
 27002                                  MAXUMB	equ	16
 27003                                  
 27004                                  ; Memory elements owned by the system are marked as PSP address 8 in both the
 27005                                  ; USA and Japan; Japanese systems also use 9 under more bizzarre conditions.
 27006                                  
 27007                                  FreePSPOwner	equ	0	; Free MCBs all have an owner PSP address of 0
 27008                                  SystemPSPOwner	equ	8
 27009                                  ;JapanPSPOwner	equ	9
 27010                                  
 27011                                  ; for LoadHigh and DeviceHigh:
 27012                                  ;
 27013                                  ;	fInHigh - Is set to 1 during HideUMBs(), and back to zero in
 27014                                  ;	          UnHideUMBs().
 27015                                  ;	fUmbTiny - Is set to 1 iff the user has specified /S on the command-
 27016                                  ;	           line.
 27017                                  ;	SegLoad - Segment address for first UMB specified; set automatically.
 27018                                  ;	UmbLoad - The load UMB number; for example, this is 3 if the user has
 27019                                  ;	          given a command-line like "/L:3,500;4"
 27020                                  ;	UmbUsed - An array of characters, each of which is 1 iff the UMB
 27021                                  ;	          matching its index number was specified on the command-line;
 27022                                  ;	          for example, after "/L:3,500;4;7", UmbUsed[3], [4] and [7]
 27023                                  ;	          will be set to 1.  All others will be set to 0.
 27024                                  ;	UmbSize - An array of words, each of which is interpereted as a size
 27025                                  ;	          specified by the user for a UMB (in the above example, all
 27026                                  ;	          elements would be zero save UmbSize[3], which would be 500.
 27027                                  ;	fm_umb - Set to the old UMB link-state (0x80 or 0x00)
 27028                                  ;	fm_strat - Set to the old memory-allocation strategy (0$00000???)
 27029                                  ;	fm_argc  - Number of arguments received by ParseVar() (see ParseVar()
 27030                                  ;	           for details).
 27031                                  
 27032                                  fInHigh:  db	0
 27033                                  fUmbTiny: db	0
 27034                                  SegLoad:  dw	0

 27269                                  multi_pass:
 27270 00001F0E 0E                      	push	cs
 27271 00001F0F 1F                      	pop	ds
 27272                                  
 27273 00001F10 803E[4903]0A            	cmp	byte [multi_pass_id],10

 27282 00001F1C 8B36[D403]              	mov	si,[org_count]

 27295 00001F39 72D2                    	jc	short endconv
 27296

 27298                                  
 27299 00001F3F C606[F713]00            	mov	byte [multdeviceflag],0	; reset multdeviceflag.
 27300 00001F44 C606[FA13]00            	mov	byte [setdevmarkflag],0	; reset setdevmarkflag.
 27301 00001F49 3C0A                    	cmp	al,lf			; linefeed?
 27302 00001F4B 7416                    	je	short blank_line	;  then ignore this line.
 27303                                  
 27304                                  ; 27/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 27305                                  %if 0
 27306                                  
 27307                                  ;ifdef	MULTI_CONFIG
 27308                                  
 27309                                  ;   If this is a genuine CONFIG.SYS command, then there should be a line
 27310                                  ;   number immediately following it....
 27311                                  
 27312                                          mov     [config_cmd],al         ; save original command code
 27313                                  	;and	al,NOT CONFIG_OPTION_QUERY
 27314                                  	and	al,~CONFIG_OPTION_QUERY ; and al,7Fh
 27315                                          cmp     byte [config_multi],0	; is this a multi-config config.sys?
 27316                                          je      short not_final		; no, line number is not embedded
 27317                                  
 27318                                          push    ax                      ;
 27319                                          call    getchr                  ; ignore end-of-image errors,
 27320                                          mov     ah,al                   ; because if there's an error
 27321                                          call    getchr                  ; fetching the line number that's
 27322                                          xchg    al,ah                   ; supposed to be there, the next
 27323                                          mov     [linecount],ax          ; getchr call will get the same error
 27324                                          pop     ax
 27325                                  ;
 27326                                  ;   HACK: when 4DOS.COM is the shell and it doesn't have an environment from
 27327                                  ;   which to obtain its original program name, it grovels through all of
 27328                                  ;   memory to find the filename that was used to exec it; it wants to find
 27329                                  ;   the SHELL= line in the in-memory copy of CONFIG.SYS, and it knows that
 27330                                  ;   sysinit converts the SHELL= keyword to an 'S', so it expects to find an 'S'
 27331                                  ;   immediately before the filename, but since we are now storing line # info
 27332                                  ;   in the config.sys memory image, 4DOS fails to find the 'S' in the right
 27333                                  ;   spot.
 27334                                  ;
 27335                                  ;   So, on the final pass of CONFIG.SYS, copy the command code (eg, 'S')
 27336                                  ;   over the line number info, since we no longer need that info anyway. This
 27337                                  ;   relies on the fact that getchr leaves ES:SI pointing to the last byte
 27338                                  ;   retrieved.
 27339                                  ;
 27340                                          cmp	byte [multi_pass_id],2	; final pass?
 27341                                          jb	short not_final		; no
 27342                                          ;test	word [install_flag],have_install_cmd
 27343                                  	test	byte [install_flag],have_install_cmd ; 1
 27344                                          jz	short final		; no install cmds, so yes it is
 27345                                          cmp	byte [multi_pass_id],3	; final pass?
 27346                                          jb	short not_final		; no
 27347                                  final:                                  ;
 27348                                  	mov	[es:si],al		; save backward-compatible command code
 27349                                  not_final:                              ;
 27350                                  ;endif
 27351                                  
 27352                                  %endif
 27353 00001F4D 88C4                    	mov	ah,al
 27354 00001F4F E87210                  	call	getchr

 27356

 27383                                  ;the first pass handles the other commands and only set install_flag when

 27392                                  	; (SYSINIT:2250h)
 27393                                  tryi:
 27394 00001F68 803E[4903]00            	cmp	byte [multi_pass_id],0	; the initial pass for DOS=HI

 27398 00001F72 803E[4903]02            	cmp	byte [multi_pass_id],2	; the second pass was for ifs=
 27399                                          ; 11/12/2022

 27401 00001F77 74E5                    	je	short coff
 27402                                  	; 27/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 27403                                  	;je	short multi_pass_coff	
 27404                                  					; This pass can be made use of if
 27405                                  					; we want do some config.sys process
 27406                                  					; after device drivers are loaded
 27407                                  					; and before install= commands
 27408                                  					; are processed
 27409                                  
 27410 00001F79 803E[4903]03            	cmp	byte [multi_pass_id],3	; the third pass for install= ?
 27411 00001F7E 7411                    	je	short multi_try_i
 27412 00001F80 80FC48                          cmp     ah, CONFIG_DOS  ; 'H'
 27413                                  	; 11/12/2022

 27417                                  	;je	short multi_pass_coff	
 27418                                  
 27419                                  ;       make note of any INSTALL= or INSTALLHIGH= commands we find,
 27420                                  ;       but don't process them now.        
 27421                                          
 27422 00001F85 80FC49                          cmp     ah,CONFIG_INSTALL ; 'I'	; install= command?
 27423                                  	;jne	short precheck_installhigh ; the first pass is for normal operation.
 27424                                  	; 27/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 27425 00001F88 752A                    	jne	short tryb	
 27426                                  	
 27427                                  	;or	word [install_flag],have_install_cmd ; set the flag
 27428 00001F8A 800E[4A03]01            	or	byte [install_flag],have_install_cmd ; 1

 27430 00001F8F EBCD                    	jmp	short coff ; 13/05/2019	; and handles the next command
 27431                                  
 27432                                  	; 27/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 27433                                  ;precheck_installhigh:
 27434                                  ;       cmp     ah,CONFIG_INSTALLHIGH ; 'W' ; signifier for INSTALLHIGH
 27435                                  ;       jne     short tryb		; carry on with normal processing
 27436                                  ;	;or	word [install_flag],have_install_cmd
 27437                                  ;	or	byte [install_flag],have_install_cmd ; 1
 27438                                  ;       jmp	short coff
 27439                                  
 27440                                  multi_try_i:
 27441 00001F91 80FC49                          cmp     ah, CONFIG_INSTALL ; 'I' ; install= command?
 27442                                  	;jne	short multi_try_n	; no, check for installhigh
 27443                                  	; 27/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 27444 00001F94 7505                    	jne	short multi_pass_filter
 27445                                  
 27446                                  ; 27/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 27447                                  ;;ifdef	MULTI_CONFIG
 27448                                  ;       call    query_user              ; query the user if config_cmd
 27449                                  ;       jc	short multi_pass_filter	; has the CONFIG_OPTION_QUERY bit set
 27450                                  ;;endif
 27451                                  
 27452 00001F96 E87AF0                  	call	do_install_exec 	;install it.
 27453 00001F99 EBC3                    	jmp	short coff		;to handle next install= command.
 27454                                  
 27455                                  ; 27/10/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS SYSINIT compatibility)
 27456                                  %if 0
 27457                                  
 27458                                  multi_try_n:
 27459                                          cmp     ah,CONFIG_INSTALLHIGH   ; installhigh= command?
 27460                                          jne	short multi_pass_filter	; no. ignore this.
 27461                                  ;ifdef	MULTI_CONFIG
 27462                                          call    query_user              ; query the user if config_cmd
 27463                                          jc      short multi_pass_filter	; has the CONFIG_OPTION_QUERY bit set
 27464                                  ;endif
 27465                                  
 27466                                  ;       The memory environment is in its normal DOS state, so do
 27467                                  ;       the standard calls to set the alloc strategy for loading high
 27468                                  
 27469                                  	mov	ax,(ALLOCOPER<<8)|0 ; 5800h
 27470                                  	int	21h			;get alloc strategy
 27471                                  	mov	bx,ax
 27472                                          push    bx                      ; save for the return
 27473                                  
 27474                                          or	bx,HIGH_FIRST  ; 80h	;set alloc to HighFirst
 27475                                  	mov	ax,(ALLOCOPER<<8)|1 ; 5801h
 27476                                  	int	21h			;set alloc strategy
 27477                                  
 27478                                  	mov     ax,(ALLOCOPER<<8)|2 ; 5802h
 27479                                          int     21h                     ; get link state
 27480                                          xor     ah,ah                   ; clear top byte
 27481                                          push    ax                      ; save for return
 27482                                  
 27483                                          mov	ax,(ALLOCOPER<<8)|3 ; 5803h
 27484                                  	mov	bx,1
 27485                                  	int	21h			;link in UMBs
 27486                                  
 27487                                  	call	do_install_exec 	;install it.
 27488                                  
 27489                                          mov     ax,(ALLOCOPER<<8)|3
 27490                                          pop     bx                      ; recover original link state
 27491                                          int     21h
 27492                                          pop     bx                      ; recover original alloc strategy
 27493                                          mov     ax,(ALLOCOPER<<8)|1
 27494                                          int     21h
 27495                                  
 27496                                  	jmp	coff			;to handle next install= command.
 27497                                  
 27498                                  %endif
 27499                                  
 27500                                  multi_pass_filter:
 27501 00001F9B 80FC59                          cmp     ah,CONFIG_COMMENT ; 'Y' ; comment?
 27502 00001F9E 740A                    	je	short multi_pass_adjust

 29071                                  ; j.k. 5/5/86: stacks=0,0 implies no stack installation.

 29073                                  ;	result in "unrecognized command" error.
 29074                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------

 29076                                  ;**************************************************************************
 29077                                  ;									  *
 29078                                  ; function: parse the parameters of stacks= command.			  *
 29079                                  ;	    the minimum value for "number of stacks" and "stack size" is  *
 29080                                  ;	    8 and 32 each.  in the definition of sysparse value list,they *
 29081                                  ;	    are set to 0.  this is for accepting the exceptional case of  *
 29082                                  ;	    stacks=0,0 case (,which means do not install the stack.)	  *
 29083                                  ;	    so,after sysparse is done,we have to check if the entered	  *
 29084                                  ;	    values (stack_count,stack_size) are within the actual range,  *
 29085                                  ;	    (or if "0,0" pair has been entered.)			  *
 29086                                  ; input :								  *
 29087                                  ;	es:si -> parameters in command line.				  *

 29089                                  ;	set the variables stack_count,stack_size.			  *
 29090                                  ;									  *

 29098                                  ;	{ sysinit_parse;						  *
 29099                                  ;	  if (no error) then						  *
 29100                                  ;	     { if (cx == 1) then /* first positional = stack count */	  *
 29101                                  ;		   p_stack_count = result_val._$P_picked_val;		  *
 29102                                  ;	       if (cx == 2) then /* second positional = stack size */	  *
 29103                                  ;		   p_stack_size = result_val._$P_picked_val;		  *
 29104                                  ;	     }								  *
 29105                                  ;	  else	/*error exit*/						  *
 29106                                  ;	     error exit;						  *
 29107                                  ;	};								  *
